messages:
maria_support: FYI ACME (customer) opened a ticket — we started seeing p95/p99 latency regressions and queueing at their requests since ~09:18 UTC. They report spikes to 10s+ and some 504s. Repro steps attached in ticket. Can SRE triage?

jordan_sre: on it. any logs or trace ids from the customer?

maria_support: customer pasted an example request id `req_20260317_9a7f`. They say it only affects their high-concurrency workload (many parallel short requests). I pasted a curl they used: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":8}' -v```

kevin_runtime: quick hypothesis: admission control is throttling long-tail bursts; could be worker saturation + KV cache pressure. Can we get recent admittance metrics for the tenant and per-worker in that timeframe?

jordan_sre: pulling admission metrics now. Initial look: hostpool-pool-7 shows sustained queue depth earlier, concurrent inflight at 320 vs normal 120. P99 token latency jumps line up with queue depth spikes.

elin_oncall: adding deploy-bot note: deploy-bot: rollback check passed (no recent model deploys in the window).

maria_support: customer insists nothing changed on their side — they had traffic spike that coincides. They need a mitigation ASAP, even a temporary workaround.

kevin_runtime: mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase per-tenant concurrency cap for ACME to reduce queueing 2) route ACME to a less-burdened worker pool (if compatible model) 3) increase worker pool size / spin up burst instances 4) apply quick admission-policy tweak to favor short requests.

jordan_sre: can we route? what model variants are compatible?

kevin_runtime: ACME uses model redwood-LLM-small-v1. There is a quantized variant redwood-LLM-small-q4a we can fallback to for CPU/GPU mismatch, but quality risk. More practical: spin up 3 warm workers on pool-9 (same model) and temporary bump tenant concurrency + allow burst. I'll open a runbook action.

maria_support: customer ok with a temporary performance-only fallback, prefers no quality regression. They asked for ETA ~ 20-30m.

jordan_sre: action plan executed: - bumped tenant concurrency cap from 60 -> 180 for tenant acme-corp (ttl 30m) - started 3 additional workers in pool-9 (warm) - enabled fairness scheduling to prioritize short requests - added circuit monitor on req latency to auto-fallback if p99 > 8s for 5m.

kevin_runtime: monitoring: queue depth declining on hostpool-pool-7, inflight down to ~140, p95 improved from 6s -> 1.1s within 6m. p99 dipping but still under 3s.

jess_acme: (customer) seeing huge improvement, thanks. We'll keep an eye and report if it resurfaces.

elin_oncall: note: created incident stub INC-20260317-ACME-QUEUEING and linked support ticket TKT-88921. Will follow up with postmortem if root cause persists.

jordan_sre: follow-ups: collect flamegraphs for pool-7 for the 09:00-10:00 window, capture admission controller logs, and check auth/billing spikes (sometimes auth retries cause fanout). Assigning to kevin_runtime + jordan_sre.

kevin_runtime: I'll gather runtime traces and KV cache stats. Early signal shows steady KV miss rate increased by ~3x for that tenant's prefix distribution which exacerbates per-request work. Could be cache invalidation pattern.

maria_support: I'll update customer w/ summary: we applied temporary capacity + fairness, monitoring improved, we will investigate root cause and revert changes after validation.

jordan_sre: agreed. leaving the concurrency bump for 30m, will start rollback plan at 1719012600 unless we see reoccurrence. Marking triage as in-progress. :thumbsup:
